I have farmed these 3 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. I never went to school, but I know this land, the weather, and what my family can manage. We are five people, and the younger ones work off-farm in the city, so I cannot take on too much labor-heavy cropping. I have a well for irrigation, but pumping costs electricity and money, so I must use water carefully and not waste it.

My plan this year is to keep 2 mu in the wheat-maize system that has always fed us and brought in cash. The winter wheat is already in the ground from last autumn. When it greens up, I will spread urea as a topdressing and irrigate three times — at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. Two pesticide sprays should be enough if the spring stays dry. After we harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize directly into the wheat stubble without ploughing. No-tillage saves time and labor, and the stubble helps keep moisture in the ground during the hot summer. The maize will need two irrigations and two sprays. 

For cotton, I will only plant 1 mu this year. Cotton needs too much hand-picking, and with my children away working, I do not have enough hands for more. I will plough that field well in spring, plant improved seed from the county supply shop, and fertilize carefully. Cotton pests are stubborn here, especially bollworm, so I will spray four times. This plan keeps us fed with wheat, earns cash from maize and cotton, and uses my well water wisely without wearing me out.
